accepted.meaning: Connectivity transition type: whether the edit repairs a disconnected parent into a connected child, breaks a connected parent into a disconnected child, or preserves connectivity; identical replacements differ because they act on different reachability regimes.

Path-count regime change: edits that collapse multiple effective paths to fewer versus edits that keep a single-path graph stable versus edits that create the first path; the same slot replacement has different structural consequence depending on multiplicity.

Whether the edited slots lie on every effective parent path or leave an alternative untouched path; identical edits are buffered when an untouched path exists and are decisive when all paths are touched.
Edited slots are co-located on a shared parent path, a shared child path, or in series; identical replacements interact differently when edits are coupled along one path versus independent.

Change in the mix of effective convolution and skip edges, conditioned on whether an unmodified convolution survives; identical replacements shift the live operator composition differently depending on remaining unmodified structure.

Whether convolution is present before and after on effective paths while an unmodified pooling edge remains; identical edits differ when they remove the last live convolution versus when pooling already dominates.
Branching/merging topology of the parent effective graph; identical replacements propagate differently through branched and merged path structures than through linear single-path graphs.
Edited edges share a source or destination node; identical replacements have different downstream reachability effects when edits converge on a common head or diverge from a common tail.
